report.title: Sol {sol} done
fail.radiation: The crew reached the radiation limit.
why.air: The crew breathes every sol. Run the air plant before the tank gets low, and keep a few days spare for dusty days.
why.food: Packed food lasts about half the mission. The greenhouse must run most sols, and the shelter only half-tends it.
why.radiation: Big solar storms add a lot of radiation in one sol. The shelter blocks most of it, but only if you hear the warning: keep the radio on.
why.blackout: Heaters use power every night. Save battery for cold nights and dusty days.

about.title: About Red Outpost
about.body: You run a small outpost on Mars for 30 sols (Mars days). Every choice costs something: power, oxygen, food or radiation. The solar storms, the radio delay, the sunlight and the ground come from real NASA data.
about.privacy: No accounts and no tracking. Your progress stays on this device.
about.ai: Built by the team with help from an AI coding assistant. Every number comes from tested code or a cited source.
about.notmedical: This is a teaching game, not medical advice.
prov.title: Where this data comes from
prov.computed: Computed in the game from cited formulas
hint.power: Each sol, choose what gets power. Sunlight refills the battery.
hint.radio: Keep the radio on sometimes to hear storm warnings from Earth.
storage.blocked: Progress cannot be saved on this device. The game still works.
const.MARS_SOLAR_IRRADIANCE_MEAN: Mean solar irradiance at Mars (used as a test check)
const.MARS_SOL_EARTH_DAYS: Length of a Mars solar day in Earth days (Mars24 step C-2)
const.MARS_SOL_HOURS: Length of a Mars day in hours
const.TT_MINUS_UTC_S: TT minus UTC since 2017-01-01 (Mars24 step A-4)
const.O2_PER_CREW_KG_DAY: Oxygen consumed per crew member per day
const.FOOD_PER_CREW_KG_DAY: Food solids eaten per crew member per day (dry, no packaging)
const.MOXIE_BEST_G_PER_HOUR: Best oxygen rate of MOXIE on Perseverance
const.MARS_SURFACE_DOSE_MSV_DAY: Average dose on the surface at Gale Crater, Aug 2012 to Jun 2013
const.RECORD_STORM_DOSE_MGY: Biggest solar-storm dose Curiosity RAD measured (May 2024)
const.CHEST_XRAY_MSV: Typical chest X-ray dose, for comparison
const.CAREER_LIMIT_MSV: NASA career radiation limit for astronauts
const.CAREERS_PER_LIMIT: The 600 mSv career limit is shared across 20 missions, so one mission may use 30 mSv
const.DUST_EXTINCTION: Sunlight lost per unit of dust opacity: transmission = exp(-0.4 * tau)
const.HAB_HEAT_LOSS_KW_PER_K: How fast the habitat loses heat per degree of outside cold
const.O2_KWH_PER_KG: Energy to make 1 kg of oxygen in the game air plant
const.O2_TANK_START_KG: Oxygen in the tank at landing (about 5 days)
const.GREENHOUSE_KG_PER_SOL: Food grown per sol with lights on and crew tending
const.EVA_KWH: Rover and suit charging for a science walk
const.SHELTER_KWH: Fans and lights in the storm shelter
const.SCIENCE_GOAL: Science sent to Earth for full marks
const.HAB_GCR_FACTOR: Share of the surface dose that reaches you inside the habitat
const.SHELTER_FACTOR: Share of storm dose that reaches you in the water-walled shelter
const.EVA_STORM_FACTOR: Being outside during a storm: extra exposure
const.STORM_MINOR_MSV: Extra dose from a glancing CME (forecast "glancing blow")
const.STORM_MODERATE_MSV: Extra dose from a direct CME slower than 1000 km/s
const.STORM_STRONG_MSV: Extra dose from a direct CME at 1000 km/s or faster (half the May 2024 record)
const.STRONG_CME_KM_S: Speed above which a direct CME counts as strong
const.SLOPE_LIMIT_DEG: Steepest ground the lander may touch down on (measured over 463 m pixels)

highlights.title: Flight Operations Systems
modal.insight.title: NASA InSight Weather Telemetry
modal.insight.desc: Real Martian weather recorded by the InSight lander at Elysium Planitia. Measures diurnal surface temperatures down to -95°C, atmospheric pressure, and dust optical depth (τ) that directly dictates solar array power output.
modal.donki.title: NASA DONKI Space Weather
modal.donki.desc: NASA's Space Weather Database of Notifications, Knowledge, Information (DONKI). Powered by the WSA-ENLIL heliospheric model, tracking real coronal mass ejections (CMEs) travelling across interplanetary space.
modal.moxie.title: MOXIE O₂ Plant & Power Microgrid
modal.moxie.desc: Modeled after NASA's Mars Oxygen ISRU Experiment (MOXIE) on the Perseverance rover. Employs solid oxide electrolysis to extract breathable O₂ from Mars' CO₂ atmosphere, balanced against habitat battery buffers.
modal.relay.title: Deep Space Telemetry Relay
modal.relay.desc: Orbital geometry calculates exact speed-of-light radio delay between Earth and Mars (3 to 22 minutes one-way). Demonstrates why autonomous habitat microgrids are essential when real-time control from Earth is impossible.
decision.title: Commander's Critical Decision
decision.storm.eva: NASA DONKI space weather telemetry confirms a solar CME is impacting Mars today! Sending crew outside on an EVA walk exposes astronauts to dangerous radiation. Do you want to shelter the crew or risk the walk for science?
decision.power.crit: Life-support blackout warning! Available power is too low to sustain all active systems tonight. Essential heaters or air will shut down unless power is rebalanced.
report.log.title: Commander's Sol Log
log.storm.eva: CRITICAL ALERT: Astronauts caught outside on EVA during CME impact! Radiation alarms sounded across the habitat.
log.storm.shelter: Commander's Log: Crew safely hunkered down inside the water-shielded bunker as the solar storm swept past.
log.storm.hab: Alert: Solar storm washed over the habitat. Unshielded crew absorbed elevated proton radiation doses.
log.power.critical: Emergency: Night power reserves collapsed! Life-support subsystems experienced temporary blackout.
log.radio.packet: Deep space radio locked onto {n} new telemetry packet(s) from NASA DONKI.
log.eva.success: EVA Report: Crew completed geological survey across crater terrain (+{sci} science).
log.science.sent: Telemetry: High-gain dish transmitted {sci} science datasets back to Earth Mission Control.
log.routine: Outpost Log: Systems nominal. Crew conducted maintenance and habitat upkeep.
briefing.title: Junior Astronaut Flight Briefing
briefing.subtitle: How NASA Keeps People Alive Off Earth
briefing.card1.title: 1. Power & Life Support
briefing.card1.desc: Sunlight is 44% dimmer on Mars and nights drop to -90°C. Heaters keep the dome warm and can NEVER shut down. MOXIE makes oxygen from Martian air, and the hydroponic greenhouse feeds your 4 crew.
briefing.card2.title: 2. Light-Speed Communication Delay
briefing.card2.desc: Radio signals travel at the speed of light, but Mars is 1.5 AU away. Warnings take between 3 and 22 minutes to travel each way! You cannot ask Earth for emergency help in real time.
briefing.card3.title: 3. NASA DONKI Space Weather
briefing.card3.desc: Real Coronal Mass Ejections (CMEs) erupt from the Sun. NASA's WSA-ENLIL model predicts their arrival. When a warning arrives, order crew into the water-shielded bunker to block lethal radiation.
briefing.card4.title: 4. Science vs. Survival
briefing.card4.desc: There is no unlimited resource mode in space. EVA walks earn science for Earth, but cost battery power and radiation dose. Every choice costs something — you're in the Commander's seat!
